practice_items.prompt: A network administrator sets up a new router and immediately connects it to the internet without changing any settings. What is the PRIMARY security risk?
options: The router firmware is too new to be stable
The router will use too much bandwidth
The router cannot route traffic until configured
Default credentials allow any attacker to log in as administrator
practice_items.explain: Default factory credentials are publicly documented; an attacker can log in without any special knowledge.

practice_items.prompt: Which action BEST describes the principle of least privilege when hardening a workstation?
options: Giving every user administrator rights so they can install updates
Disabling all accounts except the root account
Sharing a single administrator account among all staff to simplify management
Granting each user account only the permissions needed for their job function
practice_items.explain: Least privilege limits the damage an attacker can do if any one account is compromised.

practice_items.prompt: Select ALL items that are part of device hardening. (Choose all that apply.)
options: Change default passwords
Disable services not needed for the device's function
Enable full-disk encryption
Enable Telnet for easy remote access
practice_items.explain: Changing defaults, disabling unneeded services, and enabling encryption are all hardening steps. Telnet is an unencrypted protocol that increases attack surface.

practice_items.prompt: What is 'configuration drift' in the context of device hardening?
options: When a device physically moves to a new network location
The gradual accumulation of unauthorized or unintended configuration changes over time
The planned update of firmware to a new version
The process of migrating from one security baseline to another
practice_items.explain: Configuration drift occurs when small changes accumulate and unknowingly re-open attack surface that was previously closed.

practice_items.prompt: Name the term for the total set of ways an attacker could interact with or exploit a device.
practice_items.explain: The attack surface is what hardening aims to reduce by removing unnecessary entry points.

practice_items.prompt: An administrator wants to detect a brand-new, customized piece of malware that does not match any known virus definition database. Which detection method is MOST likely to identify this threat?
options: Signature-based detection
Heuristic or behavioral analysis
Hashing-based verification
Passive packet sniffing
practice_items.explain: Behavioral and heuristic analysis look at the program's actions or structure to identify anomalies rather than matching static byte sequences.

practice_items.prompt: What is a primary drawback of relying heavily on behavioral analysis for malware detection?
options: It cannot detect zero-day exploits.
It requires a constantly updated signature database to function.
It only operates when the computer is disconnected from the network.
It may generate a higher rate of false positives on legitimate administrative software.
practice_items.explain: Behavioral monitoring can flag benign administrative tools that perform system-level operations (like registry edits or process injections) as suspicious, raising false alarms.

practice_items.prompt: Select ALL functions that a host-based firewall typically performs. (Choose all that apply.)
options: Blocking unauthorized inbound connections to local services
Preventing unauthorized outbound connections from local malware to command servers
Scanning local files for known virus signatures
Filtering traffic specifically for the device on which it is installed
practice_items.explain: Host firewalls block unauthorized incoming and outgoing connections for a single endpoint. Scanning files for signatures is the job of antivirus software.

practice_items.prompt: What is the term for a security alert that incorrectly flags a harmless file or action as malicious?
practice_items.explain: A false positive occurs when normal activity is misidentified as a threat.

practice_items.prompt: An attacker abuses PowerShell, a legitimate pre-installed Windows tool, to download and run malicious code instead of using custom malware. What is this technique called?
options: Living-off-the-land
Signature spoofing
Polymorphic encoding
Heuristic bypass
practice_items.explain: Living-off-the-land attacks abuse legitimate, pre-installed system tools, making them harder for both signature and behavioral engines to distinguish from normal administrative activity.

practice_items.prompt: How does Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) primarily differ from traditional antivirus?
options: EDR only works on servers, never on laptops or desktops
EDR continuously records endpoint activity and gives responders tools to investigate and contain threats retroactively, beyond just blocking at scan time
EDR replaces the need for any signature-based scanning
EDR requires no central console and runs independently on each device
practice_items.explain: EDR builds a searchable history of endpoint activity and adds response tools like remote isolation, going beyond antivirus's block-at-scan-time model.

options: A vulnerability that has been patched for zero days, meaning it was just fixed
A vulnerability with a CVSS score of exactly zero
A vulnerability being actively exploited before any patch exists
A vulnerability that only affects devices zero days old
practice_items.explain: A zero-day is exploited in the wild before a patch is available, meaning defenders have had zero days of protection.

practice_items.prompt: Most real-world breaches exploit which type of vulnerability?
options: Zero-days, because no patch can stop them
N-days, because a patch exists but the target has not yet applied it
Vulnerabilities with a CVSS score below 1.0
Only vulnerabilities in end-of-life software
practice_items.explain: The overwhelming majority of breaches exploit n-day vulnerabilities: a patch already exists, but the target system has not applied it yet.

practice_items.prompt: Select ALL legitimate reasons an organization might delay applying a patch immediately. (Choose all that apply.)
options: The patch has not yet been tested and could break a business-critical application
Applying the patch requires a scheduled reboot that must avoid business hours
The vulnerability does not actually exist and was invented by the vendor
The organization has thousands of endpoints requiring a staged rollout
practice_items.explain: Compatibility risk, downtime, and rollout scale at enterprise size are all real reasons for a tested, staged patch process rather than instant deployment.

practice_items.prompt: A public-facing web server has a critical CVSS 9.1 vulnerability that CISA confirms is being actively exploited in the wild right now. What should happen?
options: Apply emergency out-of-cycle patching as urgently as possible
Ignore it since the server has worked fine so far
Schedule the patch for the next routine monthly maintenance window
Wait for an end user to report a problem before acting
practice_items.explain: Critical severity plus internet-facing exposure plus confirmed active exploitation is the highest-urgency combination, justifying emergency out-of-cycle patching.

practice_items.prompt: Name the term for software that no longer receives vendor security patches, requiring compensating controls instead of patching.
practice_items.explain: End-of-life (EOL) software receives no further vendor patches; organizations must rely on compensating controls like network isolation.

practice_items.prompt: Why does publishing a patch increase urgency to apply it quickly?
options: Patches always contain new features attackers want to steal
Patches disable the antivirus on the system automatically
The patch itself (or its public disclosure) reveals details attackers can reverse-engineer into a working exploit
Publishing a patch has no effect on attacker behavior
practice_items.explain: Once a patch ships, attackers can reverse-engineer the fix (or read the public CVE disclosure) to build exploit code, starting a race between defenders and attackers.
